title: 10/17 Shoot: Locked Shorts
sub: SFC, dedicated shorts. Everything Dan has locked for the 10/17 shoot from the 2026-10-12 idea rounds: 15 green screen reactions and 11 outdoor shirtless shorts. Scripted 2026-10-13.
decisions: 15 reactions are locked: 7 from round 1 and the 8 you kept from round 2.

Three of them are about looking at yourself, so each gets its own lesson: the "don't weigh me" card teaches the daily weigh-in, fat shaming teaches the shirtless mirror, Bert Kreischer teaches the weekly photo.
The Ronaldo belt clip starts at 0:05. You left that line unanswered, so I kept my reading.
The 3 outdoor shorts with notes stay as written (3 sets, cables, the abs list), because you left that line unanswered. Their notes go to the scripting task as open questions.
11 outdoor shorts are locked, with no gym B-roll. The 9 you killed are parked for the next shoot.

All 26 are scripted (2026-10-13). The filming scripts are in the shoot doc, the 15 clips are in the Reaction Clips document, and Teleprompter 2 and 3 are rebuilt. Record: Docs/SCRIPTS_1017_SHOOT_26_SHORTS_AS_DELIVERED_20261013.md.

sections.heading: Locked reactions
sections.sub: Press play and the clip starts on the line you react to, and stops where the clip ends.
sections.label: Reaction

items.t: Cristiano Ronaldo Sells An Ab Belt. It's Harder Than A Workout.
items.words: A TV ad with no speech. Now starts at 0:05.
items.what: Ronaldo's Japanese TV ad for SIXPAD, a pad that sticks to your stomach and shocks your abs.
pts: Hook: Cristiano Ronaldo will sell you a belt that shocks your abs. Here's what nobody tells you about it.
My take: these things can actually develop your abs. But shocking yourself hard enough to do it is more difficult than just working out.
Lesson: there's no saved effort. If you're going to suffer either way, do the workout.
Bottom line: skip the belt. The work is the same, and the workout is cheaper.
items.note: Starts at 0:05, my reading of "start it at 5 seconds rather than 15 seconds". If you meant a 5 second clip, say so.

items.t: Surgeons Now Carve Fake Abs Into Belly Fat. Don't Do It.
items.src: 6abc Philadelphia, "New procedure uses foam to sculpt belly fat into 6-pack abs"
items.words: Starts on "you've always wanted six-pack abs but can't seem to get to the gym". Now ends at 0:17, on "like you spent a lot of time at the gym".
items.what: A local news report on abdominal etching: plastic surgery that sculpts lines into your belly fat so it looks like a six pack.
pts: Hook: surgeons will now carve a six pack into your belly fat. It's a terrible deal.
My take: they don't build abs. They cut lines into the fat, and you still have to diet and train to keep them.
Lesson: if you have to eat right and train to keep fake abs, do the same work and get real ones.
Bottom line: there's no shortcut around your body fat.
[CLAUDE - INSERT AT SCRIPTING: what ab etching costs]

items.t: Women Say They Love The Dad Bod. They Don't.
items.src: Man vs Street, "Girls Like The Dad Bod Until We Showed Them This"
items.words: Three pieces, 24 seconds. "Do you like the dad bod?" "I'm definitely game for that." Then the picture of Seth Rogen: "he's probably not my thing." Then: "someone who still takes care of themselves, definitely strong".
items.what: Your cut: do you like the dad bod, yes. Do you like Seth Rogen, no. Then what she actually means: a strong guy who still works out.
pts: Hook: women keep saying they love the dad bod. Watch what happens when they see one.
My take: when a woman says dad bod, she means a strong guy who still works out. She does not mean a guy with a gut.
Lesson: get to about 15% body fat. That's where your upper abs start to show.
Bottom line: watch what women choose, not what they say.
items.note: 24 seconds, one under your 25 second maximum. To shorten it, drop the first piece and open on the Seth Rogen picture (20 seconds).

items.t: Bill Maher Says Fat Shaming Should Come Back. He's Right.
items.src: Real Time with Bill Maher, "New Rule: The Fudge Report"
items.words: Starts on "fat shaming doesn't need to end". Ends on "shame is the first step in reform".
items.what: The end of Bill Maher's monologue on obesity, where he says fat shaming needs to make a comeback.
pts: Hook: Bill Maher says fat shaming needs to make a comeback. He's right, and here's who you should shame.
My take: shame works. But don't use it on strangers. Use it on yourself.
Lesson: look at yourself shirtless in the mirror every morning, before you get dressed. [B-ROLL: SHIRTLESS MIRROR SHOT]
Bottom line: you can't fix what you refuse to look at.

items.t: Dr. Mike Says Tirzepatide Is A Dial For Your Body Weight. He's Right.
items.src: Renaissance Periodization, "Three Drugs Every Male Over 40 Should Take"
items.words: Starts on "tirzepatide gives you unbelievable benefits". Ends on "whatever it is you want with your body weight".
items.what: Dr. Mike Israetel on why tirzepatide (Zepbound) gives you near total control of your appetite. His other two picks, testosterone and growth hormone, stay out of the short.
pts: Hook: this exercise scientist says one drug gives you near total control of your appetite. He's right, and I'm on it.
My take: I was stuck around 190 pounds for nearly a year. On Zepbound I went from 192 to 175 in 3 months.
Lesson: it's a dial, and you have to set it right. If you're lean and just maintaining, I recommend 1 to 1.5 milligrams a week.
Bottom line: turn it up to lose, turn it down to hold.

items.t: TikTok Says Blended Oats Work Like Ozempic. They Don't.
items.src: Good Morning America, "What to know about the 'oat-zempic' craze"
items.words: Starts on "we need to lose at least 5 pounds". Ends on "losing up to 40 pounds in two months".
items.what: A news report on "Oatzempic", the TikTok drink made of oats, lime and water that people claim works like Ozempic.
pts: Hook: TikTok says blending oats, lime and water works like Ozempic, and that people lost 40 pounds in 2 months.
My take: it's oats, lime and water. That's a low calorie breakfast, not a drug.
Lesson: when something on social media sounds too good to be true, check it with AI before you do it. Paste it in and ask if there's any evidence. It takes 10 seconds.
Bottom line: 10 seconds of checking beats 2 months of drinking oats.

items.t: He Hired ChatGPT As His Coach For A Year. He's Right.
items.src: Aaron, "I Let AI Coach Me for a Year - Here's the Truth"
items.words: Now starts on "So I did what any normal person would do. I hired a coach." Ends on "Absolutely. Let's start."
items.what: A triathlete hires ChatGPT as his only coach for a year. The old cut used his verdict, which says nothing. This cut uses the moment he hires it.
pts: Hook: this guy fired the idea of a human coach and hired ChatGPT for a year. He's right.
My take: a trainer sees you a few hours a week. AI is there at every meal and every workout.
Lesson: the top 3 ways I use AI. A photo of my plate for the calories, a workout built for the equipment I have, and a picture of what I'll look like lean, at AbsByAI.com.
Bottom line: a coach who's there every day beats a better coach you see once a week.
items.note: Still not a big name. I searched for a celebrity or a major influencer taking a hard position on AI coaching and found none worth your time. Kill it if the new opening is still too soft.

items.t: Bill Maher Asks If You've Ever Seen A Fat 90-Year-Old. He's Right.
items.src: Real Time with Bill Maher, "New Rule: Fat Acceptance"
items.words: Starts on "let me ask you this". Ends on "health at any weight is an unchallenged lie".
items.what: Bill Maher on HBO: you can get away with anything when you're young, but have you ever seen a fat 90-year-old?
pts: Hook: Bill Maher asks one question that ends the whole "healthy at any size" argument.
My take: he's right, and most guys are fatter than they think. At 200 pounds I was around 28% body fat, and I thought I was fine.
Lesson: find out your real body fat percentage. At 30% your belly hangs over your belt. At 20% you look flat in a shirt and soft without one. Your upper abs show around 15%.
Bottom line: you can't fix a number you've never looked at.

items.t: There's Now A Card That Tells Your Doctor Not To Weigh You. Bill Maher Is Right.
items.src: Real Time with Bill Maher, "New Rule: Fat Acceptance"
items.words: Starts on "there's a card now that you can give your doctor". Ends on "asking your dentist not to look at your teeth".
items.what: Maher on the "please don't weigh me" cards people hand their doctors. His line: it's like asking your dentist not to look at your teeth.
pts: Hook: people are handing their doctor a card that says "please don't weigh me". Bill Maher has the right answer.
My take: trying to get abs without weighing yourself is like trying to get rich without ever looking at your bank account.
Lesson: weigh yourself every morning. You catch fat gain early, when it's easy to correct, and you see right away which behaviors cause it.
Bottom line: the scale isn't the problem. Not looking at it is.
items.note: Three locked shorts are about looking at yourself. To keep them apart: this one teaches the daily weigh-in, the fat shaming one teaches the shirtless mirror, and Bert Kreischer teaches the weekly photo.

items.t: Bert Kreischer Thought His Billboard Was Photoshopped. It Wasn't.
items.src: JRE and Friends, "Joe Rogan Gives Bert Kreischer A Reality Check"
items.words: Starts on "you thought your belly was smaller than that". Ends on "put someone else's belly on me or Photoshopped it".
items.what: Bert Kreischer tells Joe Rogan he saw his own billboard and thought they had put someone else's belly on him. He believed he was in great shape.
pts: Hook: Bert Kreischer drove past his own billboard and thought they Photoshopped a bigger belly onto him.
My take: every guy does this. You see yourself every day, so you stop seeing it.
Lesson: once a week, same spot, same light, take a shirtless photo from the front and the side. The photo shows you what the mirror stopped showing you.
Bottom line: that's the day you start. It was for me.

items.t: Kevin James Tried One Cheat Day A Week. It Wrecked His Diet.
items.src: JRE Clips, "Kevin James on Cheat Days and Losing 60lbs After Fasting for 41 Days"
items.words: Two pieces. First: "I thought you could work out six days a week and just have one day to eat what you want". Second: "your one day is going to destroy everything" through "you can't outwork a bad diet, and he was right".
items.what: Kevin James tells Joe Rogan about his "Cheat Day" documentary, and the trainer who told him one day would undo the other six.
pts: Hook: Kevin James worked out 6 days a week and ate what he wanted on the 7th. His trainer told him it would never work.
My take: the trainer was right. Cut 500 calories a day for 6 days and you're down 3,000. One real cheat day puts it all back.
Lesson: no cheat days. If you want a treat, fit it inside that day's calories.
Bottom line: you can't outwork one bad day a week.
items.note: I don't have your position on cheat meals on record. Change the lesson if yours is different.

items.t: Post Malone Lost 55 Pounds By Cutting Out One Drink. He's Right.
items.src: Page Six, a clip from The Joe Rogan Experience
items.words: Starts on "I was like 240, now I'm like 185". Ends on "soda's so bad".
items.what: Post Malone tells Joe Rogan he went from 240 to 185. Rogan: "and you did it just by cutting out soda?"
pts: Hook: Post Malone went from 240 pounds to 185, and he says he did it by cutting one thing: soda.
My take: he's right. Drinks are the easiest calories to cut, because they never fill you up.
Lesson: mine was coconut water. I drank it for years thinking I needed it. Now it's zero calorie electrolyte powder.
Bottom line: before you change one meal, change what's in your cup.

items.t: Terry Crews Doesn't Eat Until 2 PM. He's Right.
items.src: Business Insider, "Terry Crews on intermittent fasting"
items.words: Starts on "my first meal is at 2 p.m.". Ends on "I have been doing intermittent fasting".
items.what: Terry Crews explains that his first meal is at 2 PM and he eats from 2 to 10.
pts: Hook: Terry Crews doesn't eat until 2 in the afternoon. I don't either.
My take: he's right about the fast. I'd change one thing: he eats until 10 at night.
Lesson: my schedule. A salad at 2, my big meal by 6, a small meal by 9. The last meal is the smallest, and I sleep better for it.
Bottom line: fast in the morning, and stop early at night.

items.t: Alex Hormozi Asks A Fat Guy Why He Isn't 200 Pounds Heavier. He's Right.
items.src: The Iced Coffee Hour, "Alex Hormozi's advice on weight control"
items.words: Starts on "I'll ask you a better question: why aren't you 200 pounds heavier?". Ends on "you just stop at the wrong point".
items.what: Alex Hormozi coaching a host of The Iced Coffee Hour, who says he has an emotional problem with food. Hormozi: you do know how to stop. You just stop at the wrong point.
pts: Hook: a guy told Alex Hormozi he can't stop eating. Hormozi asked him one question that destroyed the excuse.
My take: he's right. You already stop somewhere. Your stopping point is just set too high.
Lesson: set it with a number. Weigh yourself every morning, and the day you're 3 pounds over, you cut back that day.
Bottom line: you don't have an eating problem. You have a stopping point problem.
items.note: The 3 pound line is my wording. Give me your real rule if you have one.

items.t: Mr. Olympia Shows The Vacuum. Here's How To Do It At Home.
items.src: Chris Bumstead, "HOW TO HIT A VACUUM"
items.words: No transcript on this one. He is shirtless from the first seconds. Pick the 10 seconds where he pulls the full vacuum.
items.what: Chris Bumstead, 6 time Classic Physique Mr. Olympia, demonstrating the vacuum. This replaces the Arnold clip, where the vacuum was weak.
pts: Hook: this is the best vacuum in the world. Watch how far his stomach goes in.
My take: you don't need to be Mr. Olympia to do it. It trains the deep muscle that pulls your waist in.
Lesson: the vacuum, one 20 second hold, with my cues. [SHOW ONE FULL HOLD, SHIRTLESS, FROM THE SIDE]
Bottom line: it's the only ab exercise that makes your waist smaller.
items.note: Check by eye. His 2021 Olympia posing routine (3.5M views) is the backup if the vacuum is bigger there.

items.t: How To Do Towel Rows (A Back Exercise With No Equipment)
pts: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or railing, hold both ends and lean back.
Pull your chest to your hands and squeeze your shoulder blades.
To make it easier, stand more upright.
items.br: Pool shot 3 (towel rows, plus the close-up of the towel around the post).

items.t: How To Do Reverse Lunges
pts: Step back and drop your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand. Alternate legs.
Beginner: hold a wall for balance.

items.t: How To Do Bodyweight Squats
pts: Feet shoulder width. Sit back like there's a chair behind you.
Chest up, thighs down to parallel.
Beginner: squat down to a real chair and stand back up.

items.t: How To Do Goblet Squats
pts: Hold the kettlebell at your chest by the horns.
Sit down between your knees, chest up.
Add push-ups, and one kettlebell gives you a full body workout at home.
items.br: Pool shot 16 (3 reps with the 50 pound kettlebell, plus picking it up).

items.t: How To Do Overhead Tricep Extensions
pts: Your triceps are the bigger muscle in your arm, and this is how you train them at home.
One dumbbell in both hands. Lower it behind your head with your elbows pointing up, then press it back up.
items.br: New shot for the pool list: 3 slow reps from the side, with a close-up of the elbows pointing up.

items.t: 3 Rules For Every Rep
pts: These 3 rules apply to every exercise you'll ever do.
1. Slow on the way down.
2. All the way through: arms straight at the bottom of a curl, chest all the way down on a push-up.
3. No swinging. If you have to swing your body to move the weight, it's too heavy.
items.br: Pool shot 10 (3 fast, sloppy curls and 3 slow ones) and pool shot 8 (push-ups with handles). I swapped the cable examples for push-ups.

items.t: Why I Only Do 3 Sets Per Exercise
pts: One light warm-up set of 12 to 15 reps.
Then two hard sets of 6 to 10 reps, with the most weight you can lift.
items.br: Pool shots 9 and 10 (side laterals, dumbbell curls) and shot 7 (kettlebell deadlifts). New shot: swapping the light dumbbells for the heavy ones.
items.note: This is your gym rule. On record, your home workouts run on a timer, not sets and reps. With no gym B-roll it has to be shown with dumbbells by the pool. If that reads wrong to you, hold this one for the next shoot.

items.t: Why Cables Beat Dumbbells For Building Muscle
pts: With dumbbells, your muscle gets a break at the top and bottom of every rep.
A cable keeps tension on the muscle the whole time.
The 3 I do every week: cable curls, cable tricep pushdowns and cable crunches.
items.br: Pool shot 10 covers the dumbbell half only.
items.note: This one cannot be cut without cable shots, and the cable machine is at the gym. Film the talking part now and add gym B-roll after the next shoot, or hold it.

items.t: Why I Do A Total Body Workout Every Day
pts: I don't do chest day or leg day. Every workout is total body, 7 days a week.
15 minutes of cardio, then 1 leg exercise, 3 upper body exercises and 1 ab exercise.
3 sets of each, and I'm done.
items.br: All pool shots: jump rope (6) for the cardio, reverse lunges (4) or goblet squats (16) for legs, push-ups (8), towel rows (3) and side laterals (9) for upper body, toe touches (5) for abs.

items.t: Why I Work Out First Thing In The Morning
pts: I used to train in the evening. Now I train at 8 every morning.
Since I switched: I'm much less stressed through the day, I eat less junk food and fewer calories, and I stopped eating late at night.
Bottom line: do it before your day can get in the way.
items.br: From the Around The House list: stepping outside into the morning sun, AG1 and the cold brew. Then any pool workout shots. No gym door shot.

items.t: Why You Must Train Your Abs Every Day
pts: Your abs are a muscle, and a bigger muscle shows sooner.
My top tier: cable crunches, leg raises, decline sit-ups, the ab wheel, toe touches and the vacuum.
Pick two, and do them every day.
items.note: Three of the six you name are gym moves. The B-roll shows the three home ones. Say so if you want the list cut to those three.
